evidence.note: Systematic upfront survey of all test files establishes the feature surface before building; ordered module build (parser→locale→engine→funcs→formats→controller→store→server→SPA) shows a coherent sense of what pieces exist and remain.

After first full run, precisely categorizes the 8 failures against 123 passing ('dependency-related (chain, diamond, cycle...), xlsx_import, lambda_via_let, oracle aggregates') — tracking done-vs-remaining reconciled against verification results, not just self-report.
Repeatedly re-runs the full suite after each fix and tracks the live pass count (131/131), using test results as the running picture of completeness across subsystems.

Periodically enumerates hidden-test risk areas (persistence, perf, spill from FILTER/SORT, xlsx round-trip of CF/validations/names) — an updated checklist of major feature families, though not a granular per-function ledger.
Notices it had silently dropped xlsx export of validations/conditional formats and goes back to add it — detects a gap rather than forgetting a whole area.
Checks len(FUNCS) but never maintains a function-by-function done/partial/not-started ledger; the ~150-function catalog is built in bulk chunks and tracked only coarsely via test pass counts.

reasoning: The agent keeps an accurate, verification-reconciled picture of major feature families and test pass counts, updates it as areas complete, and catches at least one silently-dropped subsystem (xlsx CF/validation export) — exceeding the level-5 checklist and touching level-8's reconcile-against-verification trait. But it never maintains a granular ledger of the ~150-function catalog (done/partial/not-started), relying instead on coarse suite pass counts and prose concern-lists, and there was little stuck-state to detect. That places it between anchors 5 and 8, at 6.
